subject: Client-side transfer & residency — post-demo QA and action items
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: IT Ops <it_ops@acmehealth.com>, Tony Ross <tony.ross@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T14:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up from demo — PII, retention, and deployment constraints

Ben — thanks for the product walkthrough today. Quick recap from our side and the items we need to validate before we schedule the technical deep-dive: 

- PII handling: several of our workflows ingest PHI (med record excerpts). We need confirmation on where that data can be processed (must be in-customer VPC for some flows) and whether any model KV/cache or telemetry could contain PHI.
- Retention & logs: what are the retention defaults for request/response logs and model traces? Can we set per-route retention and configure redaction at field level?
- Network boundaries / egress: for the private deployment option, we need a clear diagram showing outbound traffic flows, if any external telemetry is sent, and whether it's possible to operate with strict egress ACLs or fully air-gapped for specific workloads.
- Encryption & key ownership: do you support BYOK (customer KMS) for model artifacts and log storage? How are keys used for caching and ephemeral storage?
- Evidence: sample SOC 2 artifacts and where the audit logs will be available for our SOC/IT auditors.

I've attached our compliance questionnaire (acme_compliance_questionnaire.xlsx) — we've filled in the high-level sections. Can you please confirm whether Redwood can meet the constraints below and provide the specific deliverables you mentioned in the demo (network diagram + mapping of data types to controls)?

Desired deliverables from Redwood before the workshop: 
- One-page network diagram showing all egress paths and which components (inference runtime, monitoring, metrics) talk off-VPC;
- A table mapping data categories (PHI, PII, pseudonymized, derived metadata) to storage/retention/logging behavior;
- A short note on BYOK and whether telemetry/usage stats ever leave the VPC.

We'd like to lock a technical workshop the week of Dec 6 but can do an earlier sanity-check call if needed.

Thanks,
Sarah Jenkins
Director, IT Security — Acme Health
[sarah.jenkins@acmehealth.com]
[attachment: acme_compliance_questionnaire.xlsx]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — PII, retention, and deployment constraints

Sarah — really helpful notes, thanks for the clear list. Short recap and proposed plan so everyone has the same expectations: 

Recap (answers at a high level):
- Private/VPC deployment: supported. It's possible to configure the deployment to block all outbound egress by default; outbound integrations are opt-in.
- KV cache & PHI: we can operate with an encryption-at-rest policy and optional cache isolation/disable for routes that handle PHI. We also support application-level pseudonymization prior to send if you prefer.
- Retention & logs: default retention is 90 days for request logs, configurable down to 0; we can implement per-route retention and field-level redaction in the pipeline.
- BYOK: yes, we support customer-managed KMS for persistent storage and have integration options for HSM-backed keys in Private deployments.
- Telemetry: for Private deployments, telemetry is optional; by default no third-party telemetry leaves the VPC.

Proposed deliverables & timeline (what we'll produce before the technical workshop):
1) Network & egress diagram (PDF + PNG) showing runtime components, mandatory control-plane callbacks (if any), and recommended ACLs — deliver by EOD Dec 2.
2) Data-category mapping table (PHI/PII/other) -> storage, caching, retention, sample redaction rules — deliver by EOD Dec 2.
3) Short BYOK & telemetry note plus sample SOC 2 evidence list — deliver by EOD Dec 2.

Next steps: 
- I'll loop in Marissa (solutions eng) and Laura (legal/contract) to own the technical and compliance artifacts.
- Proposed workshop: Dec 3, 10:00 AM PT for 60–75 minutes (tech + IT security). If that doesn't work, we can move to Dec 6.

Attachments: proposed-action-plan.pdf (initial timeline + owners).

Ben Carter
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0212
[attachment: proposed-action-plan.pdf]

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Action items for ACME deliverables (network diagram + mapping)

Marissa / Laura — looping you in to execute the deliverables for Acme Health (see thread above). Sarah has provided a filled compliance questionnaire (attached by client) and is asking for a diagram + mapping by EOD Dec 2. Short asks below: 

Marissa — can you draft the network diagram and a short egress-runbook? Key inputs to ask Acme for:
- IP/subnet ranges for any on-prem connectors or proxies;
- If they require outbound internet to be blocked for production inference pods (air-gap requirement) vs. only staging/test;
- Whether they will provide KMS (BYOK) credentials or need Redwood-hosted keys;
- A list of fields they consider PHI that must never be persisted (if available in the questionnaire).

Dev — please share the minimal set of runtime components that need outbound callbacks (if any) and the port/protocols. If we can run with zero outbound for inference, call that out.

Laura — can you draft the short contractual language around retention and telemetry we can share with Sarah (per-route retention controls, redaction capability, with a pointer to SOC 2 artifacts)?

I'll host a prep sync tomorrow 9:30 AM PT to review the first draft diagrams and mapping table; workshop currently proposed for Dec 3 10:00 AM PT.

Thanks — Ben

Date: 2026-12-02T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — PII, retention, and deployment constraints

Ben / team — thanks, that plan sounds good. Quick clarifications ahead of the workshop: 

- Air-gapped requirement: a subset of our workloads (batch PHI processing) must be fully air-gapped; we expect on-prem containerization or a deployment model that ensures no outbound network connectivity for those jobs.
- IaC examples: can you provide sample Terraform snippets or CloudFormation to show VPC peering, routing tables, and egress ACLs (we want to accelerate our own review with networking).
- No telemetry outside VPC: critical — please confirm in writing that telemetry and application-level logs can be kept entirely in-customer storage and that Redwood won't ship usage metadata to third-party analytics unless explicitly enabled.

We confirm Dec 3, 10:00 AM PT for the technical workshop. I'll invite our network engineer (Tony Ross) and a security architect. If you can share the draft diagram and mapping by EOD Dec 2 that will let our team pre-read.

Sarah
Director, IT Security — Acme Health
